Today the architecture is a **shared tax-automation core with provider namespaces behind a registry**. Instead is the only registered adapter. GruntWorx already has a provider enum value, but that alone does not make it an implemented integration. Juno still uses a partly separate legacy path.

**Vendor-neutral ports**

All names below sit under `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations`.

| Port / shared service | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Authorizations::Create` | Starts the requested provider’s connect ceremony without displacing the current connection. |
| `Connections::Create` | Completes connection setup, selects the provider, binds the external account, and disconnects the displaced connection transactionally. |
| `Connections::Find`, `Disconnect`, `Renew`, `Revoke`, `VerifyGrant` | Shared connection reporting and grant lifecycle. |
| `ExportAsync` | Authorizes the export, validates documents against capabilities, creates shared envelope/send records, then delegates delivery. |
| `TaxPreparationPrefills::Find`, `TaxPreparations::*` | Shared prefill, envelope creation, deletion, and contact-merge operations. |
| `Documents::UpdateStatus`, `FailUpload`, `ResumeSends` | Shared status/failure vocabulary and recovery. The adapter translates vendor statuses before reporting them. |
| `Documents::TransferBytesToPresignedTarget` | Reusable file-byte transfer for adapters using signed upload targets. |

The core export passes **the envelope and already-created shared send records** into the adapter; the adapter owns its vendor workflow. See [export boundary](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53) and [status-reporting port](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/update_status.rb:5).

**Registration and adapter contract**

Registration is explicit and static:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = {instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead}.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = {instead: :tax_automations_instead}.freeze
```

The registry resolves a firm through `FirmSettings.provider`. It can also resolve a provider explicitly, which matters while switching vendors. For an existing connection, `client_for` derives the adapter from the connection model’s namespace, so old grants remain addressable after a switch. Unknown providers raise `UnknownProviderError`. See [Registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:3).

A registered namespace must provide the constants/services called by the core:

| Adapter member | Expected contract |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | `.for_firm(firm)`, `.usable_for(firm)`, `.capabilities`, firm-scoped querying, and the shared OAuth connection lifecycle. |
| `Client` | Shared transport/token contract; Instead subclasses `BaseClient`, which includes `TokenRefreshable`. |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, params)` |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents: ...)` |
| `DestroyForFirm` | Removes vendor records during firm teardown. |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | Removes vendor records associated with deleted envelopes. |
| `MergeForContact` | Handles vendor records when contacts merge. |

This is a convention enforced through constant lookup and method calls. `BaseClient` requires `base_url`, `auth_headers`, and `vendor_error_message`; OAuth endpoints, credentials, scope, and refresh lifetime are declared through `oauth2_settings`. Shared connection states are `disconnected`, `connected`, `expired`, and `revoked`; both connected and expired grants can be usable because refresh may recover them. See [transport contract](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/base_client.rb:3), [OAuth declaration](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/token_refreshable.rb:63), and [connection concern](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/concerns/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_oauth_connection.rb:28).

**Capability passport**

The passport is a typed, class-level description of **what the vendor accepts**, independent of a connection row:

```text
Capabilities
  terms[]
    return_type
    accepted_file_formats[]
    max_file_size_mb
  supported_tax_years[]
```

An adapter implements private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years` on its connection model. Terms can be grouped across return types and are expanded into individual entries. Supported return types are derived from those entries; a missing entry means unsupported.

Validation rejects malformed values and duplicate return-type claims. Extensions must be lowercase alphanumeric strings, file limits positive integers, and years between 2000 and the current year plus one. These checks happen when `.capabilities` is called.

Instead currently declares the same file terms across its mapped return types and computes supported years as the current year and two preceding years. The API enriches each return type into `{value, name, type, file_types, file_size_limit}` alongside `tax_years`. See [passport implementation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:20), [Instead declarations](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/connection.rb:69), and [API representation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:57).

**Data model**

| Record | Ownership and purpose |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One per firm: selected provider and external tenant/account binding. Provider values are `juno: 0`, `gruntworx: 1`, `instead: 2`. |
| `TaxAutomations::TaxPreparation` | Shared envelope addressed by firm, client, optional contact, and year; carries return type, EIN, and business name. It still persists in **`juno_tax_preparations`** and retains legacy Juno associations. |
| `TaxAutomations::Document` | Shared send record linking an original document to an envelope, provider, and return type. Provider and return type capture the send’s identity. Repeated exports reuse the same unique tuple. |
| `Instead::Connection` | One grant per firm, with staff creator, encrypted access/refresh tokens, expiry times, lifecycle state, and vendor identity. |
| `Instead::Entity` | Vendor taxpayer handle: external UUID/type, optional client/contact linkage, source, names, and sync/archive metadata. |
| `Instead::Document` | Vendor-specific extension of one shared send record: entity reference, external file UUID, and upload path. |

The shared send record owns two separate state machines:

- Upload: `waiting`, `uploading`, `uploaded`, `failed`.
- Processing: `sent`, `processing`, `processed`, `error`, `archived`, `exceeded`.

It also stores a common failure reason such as `unauthorized`, `network_error`, `forbidden`, or `encrypted`. Vendor tables therefore hold vendor handles rather than duplicating shared progress. See [shared send model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:3), [envelope model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparation.rb:3), and [Instead document extension](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/document.rb:3).

For GruntWorx, the existing seam is concrete: its enum slot exists, but it still needs a registered namespace implementing these contracts. The current connection/transport abstraction specifically assumes OAuth2 access and refresh tokens; compatibility with that assumption needs to be established for a GruntWorx adapter.
